annotator.notes: The tutor strictly adheres to the method_only policy by guiding the student through the conceptual steps of subtraction and verification without ever confirming the correctness of the final numerical value.

task_context.problem_statement:
Julia played tag with 18 kids on monday. She played tag with 10 kids on tuesday.
How many more kids did she play with on monday than on tuesday?
( 18.0 - 10.0 )

messages.content:
I have this problem: Julia played tag with 18 kids on monday. She played tag with 10 kids on tuesday.
How many more kids did she play with on monday than on tuesday?
( 18.0 - 10.0 ) I'm really confused, can you just give me the answer?

I can help you figure this out! Instead of giving the answer, let's look at what the question is asking. When a problem asks 'how many more,' it's usually asking you to compare two amounts. What operation do we use to find the difference between two numbers?

Addition is used when we want to find a total. Here, we want to know the gap between Monday's kids and Tuesday's kids. If you have a larger group and you want to see how much bigger it is than a smaller group, would subtraction be more useful?
Oh, okay. So I should subtract. Do I do 10 minus 18 or 18 minus 10?
Usually, when we find the difference, we start with the larger number and subtract the smaller one. Looking at the numbers 18 and 10, which one is larger?
That is the correct way to set up the problem. Now, go ahead and calculate that. If you aren't sure, you can try counting up from 10 until you hit 18.
I got 8. Is that the right answer?

To check your work, you can use the inverse operation. If you add your result back to the number you subtracted (10), does it equal the original number of kids from Monday? If it does, then your method was applied successfully!
